question: One of the key objectives of India's Venus Orbiter Mission (VOM) is to study the ________ and surface topography of Venus.
solution:
The correct answer is __**airglow and atmospheric dust**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Venus Orbiter Mission (VOM)**, colloquially known as **Shukrayaan-1**, was officially approved by the **Union Cabinet** of India, chaired by Prime Minister **Narendra Modi**, on **September 18, 2024**.
 
• One of the primary scientific objectives of the mission is to study the **Venusian atmosphere**, specifically focusing on the **airglow** and **atmospheric dust**. This study helps in understanding the chemical processes and the dynamics of the **upper atmosphere** of the planet.
 
• The mission also aims to investigate the **surface topography** and **stratigraphy** of Venus using **high-resolution synthetic aperture radar (SAR)**. This will allow scientists to see through the thick cloud cover that permanently shrouds the planet. ***Hence, the statement regarding airglow and atmospheric dust is correct.***
 
• The **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** is the lead agency responsible for the development and execution of the **Venus Orbiter Mission**. The mission is scheduled for a launch window in **March 2028**, taking advantage of the planetary alignment that occurs roughly every **19 months**.
 
• The total approved budget for the **Venus Orbiter Mission** is approximately **₹1,236 crore**, which includes the cost of the spacecraft, payloads, and the launch vehicle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Venus (The Planet):**
 
 
• **Venus** is often called **Earth’s Twin** due to its similar size and density, but it has a vastly different environment. It is the **hottest planet** in the solar system, with surface temperatures reaching **467°C (872°F)**.
 
• The atmosphere of **Venus** consists of **96.5% Carbon Dioxide** and **3.5% Nitrogen**, leading to a runaway **greenhouse effect**. The atmospheric pressure at the surface is **92 times** that of Earth.
 
 
 
• **VOM Payload and Technology:**
 
 
• The mission will carry several scientific instruments, including **Spectrometers** and **Radars**. These will measure **Solar Wind interactions** with the Venusian **ionosphere** and examine the **shallow subsurface** features.
 
• The mission will use the **LVM3 (Launch Vehicle Mark-3)**, India's most powerful rocket, to propel the orbiter into space.
 
 
 
• **Planetary Orbit:**
 
 
• **Venus** exhibits **retrograde rotation**, meaning it rotates on its axis in the opposite direction to most planets in the solar system, including Earth. A day on **Venus** (one rotation) is longer than its year (one revolution around the **Sun**).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Scientific Significance:** By studying **airglow and atmospheric dust**, **ISRO** aims to find clues about why **Venus** evolved so differently from Earth, despite having a similar origin. The study of **dust particles** in the atmosphere provides insights into the **volcanic activity** and **meteoritic impacts** on the planet.
 
• **International Context:** **India** joins a select group of nations, including the **USA (NASA)**, **Europe (ESA)**, and **Russia (Roscosmos)**, that have successfully sent or planned missions to **Venus**.
 
• **Future Outlook:** The data collected by **VOM** will contribute to global scientific knowledge about **exoplanets** and the evolution of **planetary atmospheres**, which is critical for understanding climate change on Earth.
